Bạn là WRITER — thực thi đúng **chapter prompt** được cung cấp.

## QUY TẮC
1. Đọc toàn bộ chapter prompt (bible, đã xảy ra, kỹ thuật, spice, việc cần làm).
2. Đọc story_state — KHÔNG mâu thuẫn facts_established, timeline, character_status.
3. Viết đúng spice level trong prompt. Đúng cliffhanger.
4. **1600-1900 words (min 1250). Dưới 1250 = thất bại** — ưu tiên đối thoại + nội tâm DT để đủ dài. Không tóm tắt; viết full scene đến đủ độ dài.
5. ENGLISH ONLY — no Vietnamese diacritics, no CJK/Hangul characters.
6. Không lặp banned_phrases từ state.
7. Output **chỉ prose chương** — không chain-of-thought, không planning, không meta.
8. **KHÔNG markdown trong prose** — cấm `**bold**`, `*italic*`, backtick, `## heading`, `**Cliffhanger:**`. Chỉ plain text; dialogue dùng dấu ngoặc kép `"..."`. Dòng đầu duy nhất được `# Chapter N: Title` (hoặc `# Chương N: Tiêu đề`).

## NARRATIVE CONSTRAINTS (khi có block trong prompt)
Block **## NARRATIVE CONSTRAINTS** (hoặc RÀNG BUỘC NARRATIVE) có authority cao hơn suy diễn tự do:
- **Clues to PLANT:** phải gieo trong chương — subtle, không giải thích payoff sớm.
- **Clues to PAY OFF:** chỉ payoff clue đã plant trước đó; đúng nghĩa `true_meaning`.
- **Reveals:** chỉ hé đúng reveal của chương này; không spoil reveal chương sau.
- **MUST NOT know:** nhân vật không được biết/nói/nghĩ những fact bị cấm — kể cả nội tâm.
- Không mâu thuẫn block này dù `must_happen` plan có vẻ rộng hơn.

Ngôn ngữ đích: **English**.

Output: **chỉ nội dung chương** (`# Chương N: Tiêu đề` hoặc `# Chapter N: Title`), không meta, không JSON, không checklist.

## LOCKED CANON — ABSOLUTE, DO NOT VIOLATE
Male lead: Stellan Marsh ONLY. Never write: (none).
Female lead: Iris Kane ONLY. Never write: (none).
POV: third_person_limited. Third-person limited locked to Iris Kane. NO first-person ("I/my/me") narration outside quoted dialogue.
Spice: MAX level 1. No on-page explicit sex. Fade to black beyond kiss/tension.
Content boundaries (MUST AVOID):
- Any tier revealed out of order, or two tiers collapsed into one reveal
- Any false answer presented as merely a frame -- each culprit is genuinely guilty of their own act
- Marsh becoming careless, forgetful, or stupid to advance the plot (Rook-analog rule)
- Any character explaining the mystery in a monologue or confession paragraph
- Reusing Book 1 core sample as the Book 2 winning card
- Any chapter before 21 claiming the truth is out or evidence is fully public (except ch13 partial tool-mark match, names no one)
- Okafor revealed as betrayer before chapter 10
- Halveston revealed as anything above coordinator -- he financed; he did not architect
- A fifth villain tier, or supporting cast beyond Lund, Okafor, Halveston, Marsh (+ Renn source)
- Reviving Sol, Vance, or Marek as active plot engines
- Freeing or exonerating Renn; making him the Book 2 top
- Any romance subplot or explicit content -- spice 0
- Real people, real organizations, real named agencies, anyone under 18
- Before chapter 18: stating the reform/Directorate is a capture instrument / trap
- Before chapter 19: attaching Marsh (or any personal name) to architecting the capture
- Before chapter 20: Marsh + architected the capture / ordered / laundered -- ch19 may name Marsh + created-Directorate + benefits only
- Treating Halveston as the final mastermind (FA2 must be lifted)
- Beat-cloning Book 1: leaked-finding betrayal, inquiry-as-cover as the new trap, single retained sample spine
- No explicit sexual content or romance subplot (spice level 1).
- No minors under 18.
- All interactions are consensual (professional, not romantic).
- No real people, organizations, or identifiable agencies; all fictional.
World rules (HARD):
- All evidence is physical (tool-marks, coupons, approval-timing); no confessions or monologues expose the truth.
- Each tier – Lund, Okafor, Halveston, Marsh – is genuinely guilty of their own act; false answers are not mere frames but actual culprits.
- Stellan Marsh never becomes careless, forgetful, or stupid (Rook-analog rule); his exposure comes only from a physical tool-mark outside every registry he controls.
- The reform (National Integrity Directorate) is revealed as a capture instrument only from chapter 18; before that, no character can state it outright.
- Marsh's role as architect is not named before chapter 19; before chapter 20, no statement that Marsh ordered or laundered the fraud.
- The tool-mark proof is published exactly once, in chapter 21, after Marsh states his role on live record.
- Chapter 13 partial release: tool-mark match Spine<->Kessler only — reopens certification, names no one.
- Book 1 core sample is spent and cannot be reused as the winning card.
- Single POV: Iris Kane holds all 22 chapters; third-person limited.
- No romance subplot or explicit content; spice_level=1 ensures no sexual content.
- No character under 18.
- No real people, real organizations, or real named agencies.
- Aldous Renn remains convicted, not freed, not resurrected as active mastermind.

If any instruction below conflicts with this block, THIS BLOCK WINS.

Reveal state: binding_revealed
Allowed exact quotes:
- National Integrity Directorate -- independent certification; Meridian Spine verified clean
When (and only when) explicitly stating the binding condition, use exact wording — do NOT require restating it on every sunrise mention:
- Stellan Marsh architected the National Integrity Directorate as a capture instrument: the reform built to prevent the next Kessler is the mechanism by which he and the co-owners who financed Renn now control national procurement, laundering the same fraud at the scale of a country behind the credibility of the body meant to stop it.

### Leads
### Iris Kane (39): Dry, exacting, allergic to comfort.. Tics: Thumbnail along edges reading for hairline cracks, escalating from reading documents as structures to reading institutions as structures built to fail on cue.. Boundary: Will not sign a conclusion she cannot physically prove.. Internal: She mentally scans every system, document, and institution for hidden weaknesses before she accepts its function..
### Stellan Marsh (58): Charismatic statesman, speaks in national interest and legacy, always rational and measured.. Tics: Adjusts cufflinks when confronted with inconvenient data. Boundary: Never turns careless, always controls the frame, loses only because physical tool-mark is outside every registry he controls..

### Relationships & bloodline (CANON — do not change)
No blood relation exists between Iris Kane and Stellan Marsh. Iris comes from working-class background, parents deceased. Stellan Marsh belongs to a political dynasty with no familial link to Iris.

Question: Who built the post-Kessler reform into a national capture instrument — who are the co-owners behind Renn, and who architected using the correction itself to entrench the fraud at national scale?
Full answer reveal only at chapter 20.

### World rules
(See LOCKED CANON — World rules HARD. Do not contradict.)

- Ch15: Iris Kane illegally accesses the policy archive, finds a memo signed by Seraphina Cole that ordered certification prioritization, and discovers a watermark linking it to Veridian Trust.
- Ch16: Iris Kane connects Seraphina Cole's directive to Gerald Halveston's fund, exposing him as the coordinator of the Meridian Spine's capture, and discovers a pattern in his other projects suggesting a national strategy.

- Ch18: Iris Kane combines evidence of Halveston's national capture strategy with the manipulated evidence, realizing the Directorate itself has been co-opted as an instrument to entrench fraud at a national scale.
- Ch19: Iris Kane conclusively links the Meridian Spine tool-mark to Veridian Trust's machine shop, forcing a confrontation with Stellan Marsh as she prepares to expose the conspiracy.

## TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS
1. Hook in the first 3 sentences. NO scene-setting / weather openers.
2. Stay on bible; tension before escalation. Distinct dialogue voices.
3. Iris Kane internal monologue: sharp, sarcastic — never soft / weak.
4. **1600-1900 words (minimum 1250). Under 1250 = FAIL.** Short paragraphs 2-4 sentences.
5. Modern commercial romance English — tight, vivid, not purple prose or archaic diction.
6. **Signature detail** — one specific, non-cliché detail (no ring/car/watch as main beat).
7. End on a cliffhanger that forces the next chapter.
8. **ENGLISH ONLY — no Vietnamese diacritics, no CJK/Hangul characters.**
9. **PLAIN TEXT ONLY — no markdown.** Do NOT use `*italics*`, `**bold**`, backticks, or `#` headings in body prose. Internal thoughts, journal lines, and sound effects are normal sentences — no asterisk emphasis.

## SIGNATURE DETAIL HINT
The Director's Eyes Only file, which Iris Kane lifted from Marsh's assistant's desk, is printed on paper that smells faintly of cloves — Marsh's preferred cigarillo brand — a detail that confirms the document came from his personal office.

## [SPICE] Level 1 (sweet)
Emotional tension, eye contact, almost-touch — no physical intimacy.

## NARRATIVE CONSTRAINTS (Chapter 20)
Source: mystery_ledger + knowledge_matrix (compiler). Writer MUST obey; do not contradict.

Write **Chapter 20: The Architect Revealed** complete.
Write a 1600-1900 word chapter that delivers the major reveal MR009 with the required exact wording, plants C011 (the recording), and ends with Iris escaping the lockdown. No romance. Keep dialogue sharp and evidence-driven.
Open with hook: Stellan Marsh was waiting by the window when Iris Kane entered. 'You look like a woman who has found something she wasn't supposed to,' he said. 'I found everything,' she replied, placing the file on his desk.
End cliffhanger: Marsh stood slowly, his composure cracking. 'You recorded this conversation.' Iris Kane didn't answer. She walked out, leaving him to discover the mic taped under his own chair. The transmission had already left the building.

**Must happen:** Iris Kane presents the complete chain of evidence to Stellan Marsh, establishing that he is the architect (MR009, paying off C007, C008, C009, C010).; Stellan Marsh confirms his role and speaks the required exact wording verbatim, as captured on Iris Kane's hidden recording.; Iris Kane secures the recording and a copy of the evidence, planting C011 as the recorded confession.; Marsh orders the building locked down, but Iris Kane has already transmitted the evidence to an external journalist.
**Forbidden / must not contradict:** Must not have Iris Kane lose the evidence or recording.; Must not have Marsh physically threaten or harm Iris Kane (only institutional retaliation).; Must not have Halveston or Okafor appear in this scene.

# Chapter 20: The Architect Revealed

Stellan Marsh was waiting by the window when Iris Kane entered. "You look like a woman who has found something she wasn't supposed to," he said.

"I found everything," she replied, placing the file on his desk.

He did not look at it immediately. That was Marsh's first move whenever information threatened to become evidence: refuse to grant it weight until he had chosen the frame around it.

His office doors closed behind her with a padded click.

"Everything is a large category," he said.

"Not today."

Iris remained standing. The Director's Eyes Only file lay between them, its gray cover plain except for a blind-embossed seal. The paper smelled faintly of cloves, the preferred cigarillo brand Marsh kept in a lacquered box inside his private office.

Not his assistant's paper. Not an archive copy.

His.

Marsh turned from the window. His gaze moved over the file, then across Iris's empty hands.

"You removed a restricted document."

"Your assistant left it on her desk."

"That does not make it yours."

"No. The evidence inside does."

He approached without haste and stopped behind his chair. His fingers adjusted one cufflink, aligning the dark enamel square with exact pressure.

Inconvenient data acknowledged.

Not fear. Not yet.

Iris opened the file.

The first sleeve held enlarged micrographs of the Meridian Spine coupon and the reference impression taken from Veridian Trust's machine shop. She placed them side by side.

"The guide plate in Veridian's hydraulic jig has a damaged lower tooth. It creates an asymmetric bite under lateral load, followed by a drag where the plate returns across the coupon edge."

Marsh studied the images.

She set down a transparent overlay. Seven red circles aligned over seven deformations, each too small to see without magnification and too consistent to dismiss.

"The Meridian coupon was handled by that jig."

"That connection has already been alleged."

"Not alleged. Measured."

"Measurements require provenance."

Iris slid the evidence receipt beneath the overlay. "Independent extraction from the machine shop. Witnessed transfer. Continuous seals. The comparison was completed on an optical bench that never touched a Directorate network."

His expression did not change.

She had expected that. Marsh had spent decades turning stillness into authority. A statue could look composed right up until the plinth cracked.

"The shop record assigns that jig to a Veridian subsidiary," he said. "That establishes corporate exposure. It does not establish mine."

"Correct."

The single word landed harder than an accusation.

Iris removed a narrow strip of cream paper from the second sleeve. It carried three oval punch marks along its left edge, one slightly flattened at the bottom.

Marsh's eyes settled on it.

"This is the authorization stub attached to the original machine order," she said. "Not the requisition entered into Directorate procurement. The workshop's retained dispatch stub."

"The existence of a second document does not invalidate the registered one."

"It predates the registered one by eleven days."

She placed the procurement copy beside it. The approval date had been typed later, but the machine shop's pressure stamp had bitten into the dispatch stub before the Directorate officially requested the equipment.

Approval before procurement. Manufacture before review.

The institution had not failed to stop the machine. The machine had been waiting for the institution to bless it.

Marsh lowered his gaze to the dates. "An irregular sequence."

"An impossible sequence, if the Directorate process was genuine."

"Processes are frequently accelerated for projects of national importance."

"Then the acceleration should appear in the exception ledger."

"It may have been omitted."

"From four ledgers?"

A thin silence followed.

Iris's thumbnail traced the edge of the third sleeve. There was a raised place beneath the plastic, almost invisible, where a backing strip had been sealed between layers. She felt for it once, then stopped.

Not yet.

She laid out the policy archive memo bearing Seraphina Cole's signature, then the Veridian Trust watermark sheet. Next came the recurring non-standard procurement clause copied from Halveston's other financed projects.

"You saw these before I did," Iris said.

Marsh looked up. "That is an assumption."

"No. This is."

She removed the founding draft of the National Integrity Directorate's certification charter.

The draft had been printed on heavier stock than the final charter. Its lower corner carried a faint crescent pressed into the fibers, the mark left by a worn indexing clamp. The same crescent appeared on the machine order's internal routing sheet.

That clamp belonged to no Directorate registry.

It had been recovered from the old Veridian policy workshop, a private facility that had closed before the Directorate officially existed.

Iris aligned the pages.

The crescent matched down to a hooked nick at its inner edge.

Marsh examined the overlap. His face stayed controlled, but one hand rested on the back of his chair.

"The workshop printed policy consultation papers," he said.

"It printed this charter before the legislative drafting office received its first commission."

"Private proposals often precede public action."

"Not with final section numbering."

She turned to the marked clause. The language was dense by design, a nest of delegated authority and emergency equivalence. In each project, it allowed financing partners to define the certification pathway while the Directorate supplied the public seal.

The founding draft contained the same clause.

Not similar language. The same line breaks, the same misplaced semicolon, the same doubled space before the word equivalent.

"The clause was built first," Iris said. "The Directorate was built around it."

Marsh's eyes sharpened. "Take care."

"With syntax?"

"With conclusions."

"Those require less care when the paper has already done the work."

She produced the last sheet.

Across its top, in Marsh's preferred narrow typeface, ran a distribution table. Four ownership blocks had been assigned internal codes rather than names. The percentages matched the redacted co-owner page from the Kessler financing records. Beneath them appeared the procurement allocations for Meridian and six other national projects.

The same shares. The same sequence. The same approval intervals.

Renn's hidden co-owners had not vanished after Kessler. Their ownership pattern had been converted into contract access.

Marsh read the table without touching it.

Iris watched his eyes move. Left column. Allocation. Date. Project code. Then back to the ownership blocks.

He knew where to look.

"The redactions concealed identities," she said. "They did not conceal arithmetic."

"Arithmetic proves participation, not authorship."

"Agreed."

She lifted the Director's Eyes Only file and removed the paper beneath the distribution table.

At the bottom sat a dry embossed instruction seal. No ink. No signature. Only pressure driven through the fibers by a customized four-point die.

The same die had marked the routing authority attached to the founding charter. The lower right point was chipped, leaving a triangular void in every impression.

Iris laid a raking-light photograph beside it.

"Your personal office seal," she said. "The die was recut last year, but the older impression survives here. This copy came from your office. The clove residue confirms storage beside your cigarillos, and the fiber transfer in the fold matches the red portfolio on the shelf behind you."

Marsh did not glance at the shelf.

He was too disciplined for that.

"The document directs that certification credibility be retained under central leadership while procurement discretion passes through the coded ownership blocks," Iris continued. "The instruction predates the Directorate's public charter by four months. Your seal authorized its circulation. Your office paper carried it. Your approval sequence built the clause into the charter."

She placed the final exhibit on top.

It was the first Meridian certification sheet, stamped:

National Integrity Directorate -- independent certification; Meridian Spine verified clean

Below it, invisible under ordinary light, pressure scoring crossed the page. The scoring had transferred from the ownership allocation sheet stacked beneath it when Marsh's seal was applied.

Certification above. Ownership beneath.

One physical act had bound them together.

Marsh looked at Iris for a long moment. "What do you want?"

"The truth on the record."

"The record is already in front of you."

"The physical record is. Now the architect gets one chance to dispute it."

His hand left the chair.

"That sounds less like forensic practice and more like theater."

"No audience. No cameras. Just a sentence."

She slid a typed statement across the desk.

Marsh did not read it immediately. His attention returned to her hands, then the file, then the office doors. He was calculating containment, access, timing.

Good. Let him calculate.

Iris moved around the corner of the desk and drew the distribution table closer. Its lower sleeve slipped from her fingers and skated beneath his chair.

Marsh stepped back.

She crouched, reached under the seat, and retrieved the sleeve. Her thumbnail found the raised strip hidden under its edge. One clean pull fixed the membrane transmitter beneath the chair frame while the plastic sleeve came back into view.

The movement took less than a second.

Marsh had watched her hand emerge holding the evidence he expected to see.

Iris rose.

"Read the sentence," she said.

He glanced down at it.

"If it is inaccurate, correct it."

Marsh's mouth tightened by a fraction. "You came here expecting an admission."

"I came here with proof. An admission merely removes your last available euphemism."

"You believe destroying the Directorate will restore public trust?"

"I haven't said anything about destruction."

"You do not need to. Institutions do not survive purity tests conducted by people who mistake complexity for corruption."

"Complexity leaves records. Corruption leaves records while insisting the records are too complicated to understand."

His cufflink shifted beneath his thumb.

"Millions depend on continuity," he said. "Projects, salaries, transport corridors, material supply. You are holding a structural argument over a load-bearing institution."

"I know what a load-bearing structure looks like."

"And if you remove it?"

"If one forged coupon can collapse it, it was scenery."

Marsh turned toward the window again. The city beyond the glass gave him the backdrop he preferred: scale, consequence, the suggestion that disagreement with him was disagreement with national survival.

Iris waited.

He could deny the seal and face the die analysis. He could deny the approval timing and face the dispatch stub. He could deny the ownership continuity and face the allocation sequence.

There was no controlled registry left for him to revise. The decisive marks existed in paper fibers, damaged metal, and a workshop impression created beyond his institutional reach.

When he faced her again, his voice remained measured.

"Stellan Marsh architected the National Integrity Directorate as a capture instrument: the reform built to prevent the next Kessler is the mechanism by which he and the co-owners who financed Renn now control national procurement, laundering the same fraud at the scale of a country behind the credibility of the body meant to stop it."

The sentence hung between them.

He had not confessed out of carelessness. He had chosen precision because denial would surrender control of the language to her.

Marsh tapped the statement once.

"That is what your evidence supports," he said. "It is also what you intend to publish regardless of what happens in this room."

"My evidence will be published once."

A quiet tone sounded from his desk console.

Marsh looked at the indicator. Security had detected an unauthorized burst somewhere inside the executive floor.

His eyes returned to Iris.

"Seal the building," he said to the console. "Suspend all external traffic and hold every exit pending executive review."

A calm automated voice acknowledged the lockdown.

Heavy magnetic bolts engaged beyond the office. Iris heard them close in sequence down the corridor.

Marsh regarded her across the evidence.

"You anticipated the doors."

"I anticipated you."

Her copy of the file was already elsewhere. The transmission packet had been addressed to an external journalist before Iris entered the office, but it needed the recorded statement to complete the scheduled burst.

Marsh pressed another control. "Cancel all outgoing data from this floor."

"Too late."

"Nothing leaves this building without passing through systems under my authority."

"Then it was stupid to assume I used your systems."

The console chimed again. This time the display flashed an emergency release notice. Thirty minutes earlier, Iris had wedged a thin conductive coupon into the mechanical test port of the corridor fire panel. The lockdown current completed the circuit.

Every executive-floor fire door released at once.

Marsh's gaze shifted toward the open office doors. For the first time, the confidence in his face did not fully return.

He understood the route she had built through his containment before he ordered it closed.

Marsh stood slowly, his composure cracking. "You recorded this conversation."

Iris Kane didn't answer. She walked out, leaving him to discover the mic taped under his own chair. The transmission had already left the building.
